papers.title: The Influence of Heat and Surface Treatment on the Functional Properties of Ti6Al4V Alloy Samples Obtained by Additive Technology for Applications in Personalized Implantology
papers.abstract: The main aim of this study was to evaluate the influence of heat and surface treatment on the physicochemical properties of samples produced using Direct Metal Sintering incremental technology from Ti64ELI titanium powder. Two groups of samples were selected for the study: sandblasted and mechanically polished samples. Each group consisted of samples in the initial state and after heat treatment carried out at temperatures of 800 °C, 910 °C, and 1020 °C. The article presents the results of microscopic metallographic observations, wettability and surface topography, hardness, and resistance to pitting corrosion in Ringer’s solution, together with microscopic evaluation of the surfaces before and after testing. Based on the test results, both heat and surface treatments were found to alter the functional properties of the printed samples. All the tested samples show hydrophilic properties. Heat treatment at 1020 °C produces the best resistance to pitting corrosion. This information is important when selecting the mechanical properties of the biomaterial and the physicochemical properties of the surface for a specific type of stabilizer. The choice of appropriate heat treatment and surface treatment of the implant will also depend on the length of time the implant remains in the body.

llm.relevance_to_user: 研究了Ti6Al4V的热处理和表面处理，但缺乏疲劳和拉伸性能数据，仅涉及硬度和腐蚀，与用户关注的疲劳/力学性能方向关联较弱。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not report fatigue or tensile mechanical properties; it focuses on hardness, corrosion resistance, and wettability, missing the core mechanical performance metrics (fatigue, tensile) required by the direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估热处理和表面处理对增材制造Ti6Al4V样品理化性能的影响
summary_zh.method: 对喷砂和抛光样品进行不同温度热处理，测试硬度、润湿性、表面形貌和耐腐蚀性
summary_zh.result: 在1020℃热处理获得最佳耐点蚀性能，所有样品呈亲水性
summary_zh.validation: 通过金相观察、硬度测试和电化学腐蚀实验验证

summary_en.motivation: This study evaluates the influence of heat and surface treatments on the physicochemical properties of Ti6Al4V samples produced by direct metal sintering, aiming to inform implant material selection.
summary_en.method: Sandblasted and polished samples were subjected to heat treatment at 800, 910, and 1020°C, then characterized by microscopy, hardness, wettability, and pitting corrosion tests in Ringer's solution.
summary_en.result: Heat treatment at 1020°C yielded the highest pitting corrosion resistance, and all samples exhibited hydrophilic behavior.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through metallographic observation, hardness measurements, and electrochemical corrosion testing.

papers.title: Effects of Ultrasonic Nanocrystal Surface Modification on the Formation of a Nitride Layer in Ti-6Al-4V Alloy
papers.abstract: This study investigates the effects of ultrasonic nanocrystalline surface modification (UNSM) on the formation of nitride layers in Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ion-plasma nitriding (IPN). Various UNSM parameters, including vibration amplitude, static load, and processing temperature, were systematically varied to evaluate their influence on microstructure, hardness, elastic modulus, and tribological behavior. The results reveal that pre-treatment with optimized UNSM conditions significantly enhances nitrogen diffusion, leading to the formation of dense and uniform TiN/Ti2N layers. Samples pre-treated under high-load and elevated-temperature UNSM exhibited the greatest improvements in surface hardness (up to 25%), elastic modulus (up to 18%), and wear resistance, with a reduced and stabilized friction coefficient (~0.55). Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses confirmed microstructural densification, grain refinement, and increased nitride phase intensity. These findings demonstrate not only the scientific relevance but also the practical potential of UNSM as an effective surface activation technique. The hybrid UNSM + IPN approach may serve as a promising method for extending the service life of load-bearing biomedical implants and engineering components subjected to intensive wear.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文主要研究表面后处理工艺，而非增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的力学或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: The paper focuses on a post-processing surface modification (UNSM+nitriding) for Ti-6Al-4V, not on the as-built or process-state mechanical/fatigue performance of additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V; it lacks any additive manufacturing context or fatigue data.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究超声波纳米晶表面改性对Ti-6Al-4V合金氮化物层形成的影响。
summary_zh.method: 系统改变UNSM参数，通过SEM/XRD/硬度/磨损测试进行表征。
summary_zh.result: 优化UNSM预处理显著增强氮扩散，形成致密TiN/Ti2N层，提升硬度和耐磨性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过实验表征（SEM、XRD、硬度、摩擦系数）验证效果。

summary_en.motivation: This study investigates how ultrasonic nanocrystalline surface modification (UNSM) influences the formation of nitride layers on Ti-6Al-4V alloy during ion-plasma nitriding.
summary_en.method: UNSM parameters (vibration amplitude, static load, temperature) were varied systematically, and the resulting microstructure, hardness, elastic modulus, and wear behavior were characterized using SEM, XRD, and tribological tests.
summary_en.result: Optimal UNSM pre-treatment significantly enhances nitrogen diffusion, producing dense TiN/Ti2N layers that increase surface hardness by up to 25% and elastic modulus by 18%, with reduced and stabilized friction coefficient (~0.55).
summary_en.validation: The findings are validated through experimental measurements including SEM, XRD, hardness testing, and wear resistance evaluation.
